source.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong benchmark design for a very recent preprint: 10 frozen research repositories spanning 10 training-algorithm families, 29 configurations of six systems, four-hour one-B300 exploration windows, clean up-to-12-hour reruns from source patches, a fixed evaluator hidden during search, and released task/evaluator/submission artifacts. The specific measurement-first/diagnose-then-intervene prescription is inferred from observational submission analysis rather than randomized as an intervention.
assessments.quantitative_result: Across 29 configurations on all 10 tasks, mean normalized score is 0.166 and the best system 0.250. Among 263 submissions that changed anything, 122 reached the learning procedure while 141 remained run-side; learning-side submissions average 0.226 versus 0.126 for the rest. More reasoning effort raises the learning-side share from 8% to 64% and mean score from 0.094 to 0.196. The paper also presents successful examples where agents first built local measurement/diagnostic rigs before algorithmic changes, but explicitly treats the learning-side score gap as observational rather than causal proof that such edits or diagnostic sequences are generally superior.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for scoring agent submissions against each frozen repository's shipped algorithm under the same clean evaluation procedure. Weak for the proposed mechanism because no matched randomization forces one agent condition to use measurement-first mechanistic diagnosis and another to intervene directly while holding effort/search budget fixed.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the benchmark claim that current agents often fail to reach the algorithmic layer and that reasoning effort changes where exploration lands. Only suggestive for the causal policy 'build measurement rigs and diagnose failure mechanisms before algorithmic intervention'.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Good: task suite, evaluators and scored submissions are reported released, and primary arXiv HTML exposes the protocol and submission classification.
assessments.external_replication: None identified; paper appeared only days before this comparator run.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence that source-code modification or more reasoning effort does not by itself imply algorithmic self-improvement; most changed submissions remain in budgets, checkpointing, hyperparameters or capacity rather than changing how the model learns.
scope_limits: Very recent preprint without independent replication.
Ten expensive ML-research repositories under one fixed benchmark contract.
Learning-side versus run-side outcome gap is observational and confounded by agent capability, task difficulty and quality of attempted changes.
Successful measurement-first examples are case studies, not a controlled diagnosis-first ablation.
The benchmark isolates training-algorithm design; not every O self-improvement problem is a model-training algorithm problem.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for AI4AI-Bench as a measurement framework distinguishing algorithmic from run-side changes; C+ for the measurement-first diagnostic intervention as a causal mechanism.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C until a matched O-relevant self-improvement task compares diagnosis/measurement-first versus direct intervention under fixed exploration and final held-out evaluation budgets.

source.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong current preprint with 26 scenarios/204 episodes, ordered fresh-session sequences, matched retained-experience on/off conditions, seven base models, four agent frameworks, mechanism telemetry, five targeted Hermes+ interventions and component/focused interaction diagnostics. The authors explicitly avoid claiming clean causal proof from every component comparison and report model/capability-dependent transfer.
assessments.quantitative_result: Persistence produces positive overall gaps across the reported Hermes configurations, including GLM-5.1 +0.20, Kimi K2.6 +0.17 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro +0.17, with other tested models similarly positive. On MiniMax, single-mechanism results align with targeted diagnoses: retrieval gate E4 has the largest single Info gap (+0.17), closeout E5 the strongest single Update gap (+0.16), and full Hermes+ reaches Update +0.24. However interaction diagnostics are non-monotonic: focused Procedural full Hermes+ is +0.085, removing E2 rises to +0.108, while removing E5 falls to +0.042. Transfer is also not uniform: Hermes+ improves several model configurations but slightly regresses DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Claude Opus 4.6 relative to their Hermes baselines.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good for the core question because later fresh-session behavior is measured under matched persistence-on/off conditions, and several mechanism additions/removals are compared. Some focused leave-one-out analyses use small scenario subsets and component interactions mean the full five-part pathway cannot be interpreted as five independent additive causal effects.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate. The benchmark directly supports checking whether persistence is actually written, rendered, routed, consulted and updated rather than assuming stored state helps. Specific Plan/Render/Route/Gate/Close interventions have diagnostic component evidence but interact and do not form a universally monotonic stack.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Good: code is linked and primary arXiv HTML exposes detailed tables, mechanism scores and interaction diagnostics.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence that persistence availability and useful pathway execution are different variables, and that adding a persistence component can help one capability while hurting another.
scope_limits: Personal-agent persistence scenarios rather than general scientific self-improvement.
Recent preprint with no independent replication.
Some component interactions are diagnosed on focused small subsets and should not be promoted to full-benchmark causal laws.
Overall Hermes+ gain over Hermes can be smaller than run-to-run variation in some comparisons.
The five Hermes+ interventions are implementation-specific, not a proven minimal pathway ontology.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for using matched persistence-on/off plus explicit pathway telemetry and targeted mechanism checks to evaluate persistent-agent improvement.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- until O-specific persistence/state pathways are tested with matched on/off conditions and capability-specific regression checks rather than importing Hermes+ components wholesale.

source.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary study with public code, explicit self-improvement and open-ended-archive ablations, two coding benchmarks, alternative greedy comparison, multiple-run Polyglot reporting, feature transfer across models/tasks and a detailed fixed outer exploration process. It is costly/domain-specific and no independent replication was identified in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: The revised paper's ablation table reports DGM 50.0% SWE-bench / 38.0% Polyglot versus 23.0% / 14.0% without open-ended exploration, 39.0% / 28.0% without self-improvement, and 39.7% / 30.0% for a greedy archive policy. The paper also reports DGM improving the original base from 20.0%→50.0% on SWE-bench and 14.2%→30.7% on the broader Polyglot reporting, and demonstrates transfer to different foundation models. A single SWE-bench DGM run is estimated at about $22,000 versus about $10,000 for the simpler ablation runs.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for the archive/open-ended-exploration component at the scaffold level: without-open-ended exploration always self-modifies the latest still-functional agent, while DGM retains a selectable archive; a greedy archive comparison provides an additional control. Compute is not identical in dollar cost across all conditions, which complicates strict efficiency attribution.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for preserving/selecting diverse archived stepping stones versus latest-lineage or greedy policies in the tested coding-evolution system. The outer archive maintenance/parent-selection algorithm itself is fixed rather than self-improved, and the exact value of archive diversity versus extra exploration compute is not perfectly isolated.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Good: public code, detailed algorithms/ablations and revised full-text HTML. Independent reproduction was not performed here.
assessments.external_replication: No independent direct replication identified; later GEA work supplies conceptually aligned but not independent same-method replication.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence within this substrate that single-lineage latest-only self-modification can get trapped after degrading steps and that useful innovations may require temporary performance dips/alternative implementations.
scope_limits: Coding-agent evolution on SWE-bench/Polyglot, not scientific discovery or arbitrary O components.
High cost and unequal overall run cost complicate direct efficiency comparison.
The search/archive meta-process remains human-fixed in this version.
Open archives can retain harmful or obsolete branches and require evaluation/provenance discipline.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for open archive/open-ended stepping-stone retention in the DGM coding-agent evolution setting.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for preserving diverse O candidate lineages until a cheaper matched O-relevant experiment compares archive, latest-only and greedy-best policies at controlled evaluation/search budget.

source.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning

assessments.primary_source_quality: High source maturity: peer-reviewed ICLR 2026 conference paper with released code and six-task evaluation. The mechanism bundles natural-language reflection, targeted prompt mutation, trajectory use and Pareto-frontier combination, so the headline comparison does not isolate reflection or Pareto preservation individually.
assessments.quantitative_result: Across six tasks, the ICLR abstract reports GEPA outperforming GRPO by 6 percentage points on average and up to 19pp while using up to 35× fewer rollouts. It also exceeds MIPROv2 by over 10pp, including +12pp on AIME-2025, and reports promising inference-time code-optimization search results.
assessments.matched_baseline: Useful high-level comparisons against GRPO and MIPROv2, but these methods optimize with different learning objects and rollout accounting. The source abstract does not establish a clean reflection-vs-scalar-only or Pareto-vs-best-only ablation sufficient to attribute the full effect to the worker's exact proposed mechanism.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for the bundled GEPA reflective prompt-evolution method; weak-to-moderate for any individual component and for transfer from prompt optimization to broader self-revision/agent policy evolution.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong relative to many agent papers: peer-reviewed venue and public code. This comparator verified the primary conference abstract but did not independently run the benchmark suite.
assessments.failure_evidence: The results show scalar-reward RL is not automatically the most rollout-efficient optimization substrate for language-interpretable control artifacts, but do not establish prompt evolution as a universal replacement for RL.
scope_limits: Prompt/system optimization rather than weight-level recursive self-improvement.
Headline rollout-efficiency comparison depends on task and accounting conventions.
Reflection and Pareto-frontier preservation are bundled.
Six tasks are broad enough for a signal but not a universal agent-improvement guarantee.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B/B+ for GEPA as a bundled prompt-evolution optimizer under the reported six tasks; B or lower for attributing gains specifically to rich reflection plus Pareto retention.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- until an O-relevant prompt/context-policy optimization experiment separately tests rich trajectory feedback and candidate-frontier retention under matched evaluation budget.

source.title: MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research

assessments.primary_source_quality: High source maturity: published at ICML 2026 with official Google Research page, public code, 75 MLE-Bench competitions, 24-hour budget, three-run mean±SEM tables and controlled reruns of open-source baselines under the same hardware/model environment. The candidate of interest—cross-branch comparative reflective memory—is one of three major pillars and is not cleanly isolated by the headline system comparison.
assessments.quantitative_result: Under the controlled Gemini-3-Pro-Preview setup, the paper reports MARS any-medal 56.0±1.5% and MARS+ 62.7±0.8%, versus controlled AIRA-dojo 37.8±2.5% and AIDE 32.4±2.5%. MARS records a lesson-utilization rate of 65.8±1.1% and cross-branch lesson-transfer rate 63.0±1.8%. The paper additionally audits 3,611 distilled lessons with an LLM and reports 88.34% attribution accuracy, with a 20-lesson human subset yielding 90% causal-accuracy agreement. These are strong system/provenance measurements but not an isolated causal uplift from reflective memory.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for MARS as an overall autonomous AI-research framework versus controlled open-source baselines. Weak for cross-branch reflective memory itself because MARS also changes budget-aware MCTS, modular construction and task-specific MLE components, and MARS+ is not a single reflective-memory toggle.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Suggestive-to-moderate for cross-branch lesson reuse. The 63% statistic shows utilized lessons often originate from other branches, and lesson audits support attribution quality, but neither proves those transferred lessons caused the aggregate MARS/MARS+ score uplift compared with an otherwise identical no-transfer memory.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong: peer-reviewed paper, public code, controlled evaluation table, explicit MLE-Bench protocol and lesson-provenance metrics. The comparator directly inspected primary PDF pages for the controlled table and lesson-transfer/audit results.
assessments.external_replication: No independent direct replication of the reflective-memory component identified.
assessments.failure_evidence: The paper's framing and lesson audits support the difficulty of credit assignment in expensive ML experimentation, but do not establish that every cross-branch transfer is beneficial or safe.
scope_limits: Composite framework with multiple simultaneous mechanisms and task-specific components.
Cross-branch lesson provenance is not causal uplift.
Lesson causal-accuracy audit relies primarily on another LLM, with only a small human subset.
MLE-Bench automated competition engineering differs from open-ended scientific mechanism discovery.
Current public leaderboard status should not be inferred from the paper's contemporaneous SOTA wording.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A-/B+ for the full MARS system under the controlled MLE-Bench comparison; C+ for the narrower claim that comparative cross-branch reflective memory is the causal mechanism behind the gain.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C until O/external research directly compares provenance-preserving cross-branch lesson transfer against no-transfer/within-branch-only memory with matched search budget and negative-transfer measurement.

cross_source_synthesis: The strongest isolated self-improvement mechanism in this batch is DGM's open archive because it has direct latest-only, no-self-improvement and greedy archive ablations. GEPA and MARS have stronger publication maturity but more bundled causal attribution for the specific worker-proposed components.

PAST-Bench is valuable mainly as an evaluation methodology: matched persistence-on/off plus pathway telemetry can distinguish stored state from behaviorally effective state, and its own component interactions warn against additive mechanism assumptions.
AI4AI-Bench strongly measures an algorithmic-layer exploration deficit but does not causally establish the measurement-first intervention inferred from successful examples.

Cross-branch or Pareto/archive retention repeatedly correlates with better search outcomes, but unrestricted information sharing should still be tested for negative transfer and independence loss rather than promoted as universally beneficial.
